result.title: Pristine Models
result.summary: Training on broad, unfiltered data enables high-quality image generation, but can also teach models concepts that should not be generated; restricting the training data ensures safety, but reduces quality because examples containing unsafe concepts also provide useful knowledge that is not itself unsafe. Existing approaches largely address this trade-off post hoc through concept unlearning, which can lead to catastrophic forgetting as the number of concepts to remove grows. We instead ask whether unsafe concept knowledge can be compartmentalized during pretraining so that access to it can be disabled at inference. We introduce Pristine Models, a novel text-to-image generation architecture with an attention mechanism that encourages the separation of safe and unsafe knowledge into independently parameterized branches. The branch-specific parameters are learned during training, while the unsafe branch can be detached at inference. On ImageNet, Pristine Models enable safer generation while retaining much of the utility of full-data pretraining, achieving higher image quality and better text alignment than training only on safe data or applying post-hoc concept removal. We further scale our approach to CC12M, demonstrating that it remains effective in a substantially larger and more diverse open-world pretraining setting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Pristine Models，一种 text-to-image 架构，通过注意力机制在预训练中将安全与不安全概念知识分离到独立参数分支，推理时可断开不安全分支，以兼顾生成安全性与全数据预训练的质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究目标是图像生成中的概念隔离与安全生成，不涉及 VLM 的视觉推理状态、证据使用或 latent 生成；「分支可断开」虽属训练期知识分离，但与推理期状态更新或视觉信息保留没有可核查的方法联系，故排除。
